hints.title: Chain-Antichain Duality
hints.text: According to Dilworth's theorem, the minimum number of strictly increasing subsequences needed to partition a sequence equals the length of its longest non-increasing subsequence.

hints.title: Reverse Sequence Reduction
hints.text: Finding the longest non-increasing subsequence of an array is equivalent to finding the longest non-decreasing subsequence of its reversed counterpart.

hints.title: Patience Sorting Mechanics
hints.text: Process the reversed array elements using upper bound searches to maintain active pile tails in logarithmic steps.

hints.title: Reference Implementation

complexity.notes: Binary search on tail array takes logarithmic time per element.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simulating repeated removals of greedy increasing subsequences takes O(n^2) and fails to guarantee global minimum partition size.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Tails array stores at most n elements.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Applies Dilworth's theorem to reduce chain partition into longest non-increasing subsequence.
